title: Investigation of stress and recovery in mothers of moderate to late preterm infants using smartwatch technology
summary:
The birth of a premature baby places considerable psychological and physical strain on mothers. This can lead to challenges with breastfeeding, increased stress and a higher risk of postpartum depression (PPD). Studies show that up to 40% of mothers of premature babies suffer from PPD – a significantly higher rate than mothers of full-term babies. The impact of these stresses on maternal health has not been adequately studied due to a lack of objective measurement methods, which makes early diagnosis and targeted support difficult.
This study takes an innovative approach to measuring maternal stress through continuous physiological measurements using smartwatches and supplementary questionnaire surveys. By combining smartwatch measurements with standardised questionnaires, the study offers a unique opportunity to objectively assess the impact of stress on mothers. At the same time, this approach allows individual differences in stress processing and specific stress situations to be identified. A better understanding of maternal stress in the postpartum period is essential for improving the long-term health and bonding of mother and child.

interventions.name: Mothers of moderate to late preterm infants who wear a smartwatch from day 2-4 postpartum for a measurement period of 10 days.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• ≥ 18 years of age
• Giving birth in hospital (study site)
• Late preterm infant (32 to 36+6 weeks of gestation)
• Informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Mothers
• After breast surgery
• With glandular hypoplasia
• Who gave birth outside the above-mentioned facility
• Who are unwilling to breastfeed after perinatal counselling
• With poor German language skills (<A1 level)
• Multiple births.

Children of mothers
• With genetic syndromes
• Osteoarticular diseases or fractures
• Palliative care
• Intensive care during the measurement period with a smartwatch
